title: pdist2
summary: Compute pairwise distances between two sets of observations.

gpu_support.notes: GPU inputs are gathered to host. Pairwise distance kernels run on CPU.

description: `pdist2(X,Y)` returns a `size(X,1)` by `size(Y,1)` matrix of distances between rows of `X` and rows of `Y`.
behaviors: `X` and `Y` must be real numeric vectors or 2-D matrices with the same number of columns.
The default metric is Euclidean distance.

`pdist2(X,Y,"seuclidean",S)` accepts a standard-deviation vector and defaults to scale estimated from `X`. `pdist2(X,Y,"mahalanobis",C)` accepts a symmetric positive definite covariance matrix and defaults to covariance estimated from `X`.
`"Smallest",K` and `"Largest",K` return the K smallest or largest distances per row of `Y`. `[D,I] = pdist2(...)` also returns one-based row indices from `X` for the selected distances.

examples.description: Keep nearest distances per query row
examples.output: D is a 1-by-size(Y,1) matrix of nearest distances; I contains row indices from X.

faqs.question: Does `Smallest` return indices?
faqs.answer: Yes. Request `[D,I]` to receive one-based row indices from `X`, matching MATLAB's nearest-distance output form.

faqs.question: Are custom distance functions supported?
faqs.answer: No. RunMat currently supports the standard named numeric distance metrics.
